text:
Jamie Benn played ten minutes on Saturday, and it was enough. Late in the second period, with the game scoreless, he snapped in a pass from Justin Hryckowian for his 1,000th career point, every one of them in a Dallas sweater. He had come close on Thursday against Winnipeg in an 8-3 loss that nobody in Dallas wants to remember. This one was the right night for it: a 2-0 win and a full building.

The goal came at 16:23 of the second, a period the Stars owned on chances (1.59 expected goals to 0.41), and it moved their win chance from 52% to 74%. Benn had been robbed earlier in the same period by Alex Lyon on a 31% look, the best chance that didn't go in. Wyatt Johnston added a power-play goal with 42 seconds left to close it out.

Jake Oettinger was the reason Buffalo never got level. He stopped all 22 shots, 2.8 goals better than those shots usually allow, and added more to the win than anyone else on the ice by our measure. The Sabres pushed hard in the third (1.57 expected goals to 1.03), and his best stop came on Jason Zucker with about 13 minutes left. Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon noted that Oettinger has now shut out Buffalo in both meetings this season, and that the Sabres only played with real urgency in the third. Buffalo went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 1.50 expected goals from those chances.

Lyon was good in defeat, 28 saves on 30 shots and the third star. He told reporters, per Yerdon, "Can't bullshit the position we're in." The Sabres are winless in four (0-3-1). Dallas, playing without Miro Heiskanen and now Lian Bichsel for at least two weeks, hosts Florida tonight.
headline: Jamie Benn gets to 1,000, and Oettinger shuts the door
